clue.text: Select fish for preserving

parts.note: to select is to pick
the ling is a long-bodied sea fish related to the cod

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a fish to put in brine or vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping food in vinegar or brine is a way of preserving it.

clue.text: " Fit to drink ", indicates River Board

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: A water authority declaring the supply safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Water described as drinkable is safe to consume.

clue.text: Both crime and criminal can .' be this

definitions.text: Both crime and criminal can .' be this

parts.words: Both crime and criminal can .' be this
parts.note: an offence is carried out, and an offender is sent to prison or for trial: one past participle covers both

explanation.surface: A remark on what offences and offenders share.
explanation.walkthrough: A crime is committed when done; a criminal is committed when sent to jail or to a higher court. The stray marks in the held text are print specks.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both perpetrating an offence and consigning someone to custody.

clue.text: Girl for whom the French- Venetian artist lacks point

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: lacks means the painter's name is missing the compass letter

parts.note: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A girl for whom a French painter from Venice misses the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes N (a compass point) from TITIAN to leave TITIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Stingy contributors to Ophelia's garlands

parts.note: in Hamlet Ophelia drowns wearing 'fantastic garlands' of crow-flowers, daisies and a stinging weed; stingy here means able to sting, not mean

explanation.surface: Miserly donors to a Shakespearean heroine's flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Gertrude's speech in Hamlet lists the flowers: 'crow-flowers, nettles, daisies, and long purples'. 'Stingy' reads as mean but means stinging.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging weeds named in Gertrude's speech formed part of the drowned girl's wreaths.

clue.text: In which its use is unlikely to be Judicially allowed

definitions.text: In which its use is unlikely to be Judicially allowed

parts.words: In which its use is unlikely to be Judicially allowed
parts.note: a court sitting in private, in the Latin phrase for that, is a hearing where a photographic device would hardly be permitted: 'its' is the device itself

explanation.surface: A remark about what the courts will and will not permit.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearings held privately are said to be 'in camera', and British courts have long banned photography, so the device named by the phrase is also the thing barred.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for a closed hearing names the picture-taking device that a judge would refuse in court.

clue.text: Easily gallops round one's boxes

indicators.note: round means the gallop word surrounds the letters for one's

parts.note: a canter is an easy gallop
one is I, and one's is I plus S

explanation.surface: A horse that races comfortably round a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Canisters are small metal containers, so the plural means boxes.

clue.text: Eat in a place in Sicily

parts.note: to mess is to eat together, as in an officers' mess

explanation.surface: A suggestion to dine at a spot in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a port city in north-east Sicily.

clue.text: French wine -in student frolics? Wild talk! $

indicators.note: in means the wine word is placed inside the frolics word

parts.note: a rag is a British students' charity carnival with pranks
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: Drunken students babbling during their pranks.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG is the British student charity week of stunts and japes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravings are incoherent or delirious utterances, the speech of someone wild.

clue.text: The only thing Lord Darling. -ton couldn't resist

definitions.text: The only thing Lord Darling. -ton couldn't resist

parts.words: The only thing Lord Darling. -ton couldn't resist
parts.note: Lord Darlington in Oscar Wilde's Lady Windermere's Fan says he can resist everything except one thing: the lure of the forbidden

explanation.surface: A line about a lord's single weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Wilde's: 'I can resist everything except temptation', spoken by Lord Darlington in Lady Windermere's Fan; the word break in the print is just the line end.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing Wilde's character says he cannot resist is the pull of enticement itself.

clue.text: Except the end of this greeting

indicators.note: the end of the word this means only its final letter is taken

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting 'hail'

explanation.surface: Someone making an exception for how a salutation finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Save as a preposition means but or apart from, as in 'all save one'.

clue.text: City style in order amongst sailors

parts.note: Bristol is a port city in south-west England
a fashion is a style

explanation.surface: A city's way of dressing, as judged among seafarers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the naval phrase 'shipshape and Bristol fashion', meaning neat and orderly; Bristol was a great sailing port.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautical idiom describes a vessel kept tidy and properly arranged.

clue.text: Catches vex parents

indicators.note: to vex is to trouble or disturb, so the letters of the next word are stirred up

explanation.surface: Children's mischief annoying their mother and father.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap something is to catch it, so a verb meaning snares fits catches.

clue.text: Extraction from part of a book about a landlord's income

indicators.note: about means the book part goes around the other letters

parts.note: a page is part of a book
rent is what a landlord collects

explanation.surface: A passage taken from a book on a property owner's earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraction means descent or origin, as in 'of Irish extraction', which is one's lineage.

clue.text: Put back the lattice-work — one has left it to fall back

indicators.note: putting something back here means reading the remaining word in the opposite direction
one has left means the letter standing for one departs from the word

parts.note: an espalier is a lattice on which fruit trees are trained flat
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A gardener's trellis, abandoned, collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' turns round ESPALER, which is ESPALIER after 'has left' removes I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slip back into an earlier, worse state, such as an illness.

clue.text: Doggedly continued giving stray pets rides

indicators.note: stray suggests wandering out of place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly giving rides to stray animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on stubbornly is to keep going despite difficulty.

clue.text: Among active men the theologian trembles

indicators.note: among means the theologian's letters sit within the word for active men

parts.note: doers are people who act rather than talk
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a theologian

explanation.surface: A divine shaking among men of action.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who totters with age is shaky on their feet, so the verb means trembles.

clue.text: Complex character needed to solve' a riddle

definitions.text: Complex character needed to solve' a riddle

parts.words: Complex character needed to solve' a riddle
parts.note: the Theban king of myth answered the Sphinx's riddle, and Freud named a psychological complex after him

explanation.surface: A complicated person required to crack a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' suggests complicated, but points to Freud's Oedipus complex; the king solved the Sphinx's riddle about man.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Theban king both lends his name to a complex and solved the Sphinx's puzzle.

clue.text: Merit being severed in pieces ?

indicators.note: in pieces means the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Asking whether worth survives being cut apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to earn it or be worthy of it.

clue.text: Macbeth meant to be doubly 'so about Macduff

definitions.text: Macbeth meant to be doubly 'so about Macduff

parts.words: Macbeth meant to be doubly 'so about Macduff
parts.note: in Shakespeare's play Macbeth vows to 'make assurance double sure' by killing Macduff, so he wished to be twice certain

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean villain wanting double certainty about a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth Act 4 the king, though told no man born of woman can harm him, resolves to 'make assurance double sure' and kill Macduff anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means certain or confident, the state Macbeth wanted to make doubly secure.

clue.text: " A lily on thy brow, with — moist and fever dew" (Keats)

definitions.text: " A lily on thy brow, with — moist and fever dew" (Keats)

parts.words: " A lily on thy brow, with — moist and fever dew" (Keats)
parts.note: the missing word is from Keats's La Belle Dame sans Merci, describing the knight's pale suffering brow

explanation.surface: A line from a Keats ballad with one word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's La Belle Dame sans Merci reads 'I see a lily on thy brow, With anguish moist and fever dew'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap is filled by the poem's word for deep distress, which dampens the knight's brow.

clue.text: Climb on the North east — with all sides different

parts.note: to scale is to climb
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a north-east face, a lopsided one.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalene triangle has three unequal sides.

clue.text: Is poor Ned glad to be sus : pended ?

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a man named Ned is happy to be hung up.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon in the held text is a print speck at the line break of 'suspended'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hung loosely so as to swing describes something left hanging, as a suspended object is.

clue.text: Do site training in new form of breakdown

indicators.note: putting words in a new form means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A building-site training course that falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling to pieces is a collapse, the same as a breakdown.

clue.text: One of the Black Prince's Crécy winnings

definitions.text: One of the Black Prince's Crécy winnings

parts.words: One of the Black Prince's Crécy winnings
parts.note: at the battle of Crécy in 1346 the young Black Prince was said to have won his knightly ...

explanation.surface: A trophy taken by Edward the Black Prince at a famous battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward III reportedly told his men to 'let the boy win his spurs' at Crécy; a knight's spurs marked his knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight's prized heel-spike was the token of the honour gained in battle.

clue.text: Natural, perhaps, but unintended

definitions.meaning: in music a natural sign is one of the marks altering a note outside the key signature

explanation.definitionFit: In music a natural, like a sharp or flat, is a sign added before a note; and anything happening by chance is unplanned.

clue.text: Note on German town made by an old Jew

indicators.note: on means the note is placed after the town's name

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A remark about a German town written by an ancient Hebrew.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic sect of Jews in ancient Judea.

clue.text: Like the Labyrinth but not Cleopatra's Needle

definitions.text: Like the Labyrinth but not Cleopatra's Needle

parts.words: Like the Labyrinth but not Cleopatra's Needle
parts.note: Theseus ran a line of yarn through the Cretan maze, while the London obelisk, despite its name, has no eye for yarn

explanation.surface: A comparison of two ancient monuments.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariadne gave Theseus a ball of thread to find his way out of the Labyrinth; Cleopatra's Needle is a stone obelisk on London's Embankment, so no thread passes through it.
explanation.definitionFit: The maze had a string laid through it, while a needle in name only never took any yarn.
